answer: Agents surveying a hollow, monitoring willow health or inspecting a jetty can rotate keys without gaining extra reward claims. An issuer checks people in person and issues one credential per person, rejecting duplicate enrollments. For each claim, a zero-knowledge proof ties a valid credential to H(its_secret, epoch) and the payout key. The ledger pays each tag once, across every alias. Extra payouts require recruiting more enrolled people or compromising their credentials. Security depends on reliable enrollment and sound proofs.
